name: Flat White
intro: A flat white is a small, velvety drink where a double espresso meets glossy, finely textured milk. The coffee flavor stays front and center, with a smooth, sweet creaminess that feels rich without being heavy. It's for people who want a latte's comfort with a cappuccino's coffee punch.
heroAlt: Engraved line illustration of a flat white with microfoam

vessel.name: Small ceramic cup
vessel.note: The coaster recipe totals 6 oz, so a 6 oz cup keeps the ratio right.

ingredients.note: From roughly 18 g of finely ground coffee.
Whole milk, textured into silky microfoam with very little visible foam.

equipment.alternative: Moka pot or AeroPress plus a handheld frother (see home methods)
Stop when the pitcher is hot to hold for just a couple of seconds

steps.title: Warm the cup
steps.body: Preheat your small cup with hot water. With only 6 oz of liquid, a cold cup takes a surprising amount of heat out of the drink.

steps.title: Pull a strong double
steps.body: Pull a double shot into the cup. Because there is little milk, the espresso must taste good on its own. Sour or harsh shots stand out in a flat white.
steps.tip: If it tastes thin, try a slightly finer grind.

steps.title: Measure the milk
steps.body: Pour about 4 oz of cold milk plus a splash extra into a small, cold pitcher. A small pitcher lets you control a small amount of milk.

steps.title: Barely stretch
steps.body: Keep the wand tip just below the surface and add air for only a second or two. You want to gently expand the milk, not make visible foam. Less air is what gives a flat white its smooth, flat surface.
steps.tip: The milk should sound like a quiet hiss, not a loud slurp.

steps.title: Texture to silk
steps.body: Sink the wand and create a whirlpool, heating to about 130 to 140°F. The spin breaks air into tiny bubbles, making microfoam that looks like wet paint. Stop heating before it gets too hot to hold.
steps.tip: If you see big bubbles, tap the pitcher firmly and swirl until glossy.

steps.title: Pour with care
steps.body: Pour in a steady, low stream so the espresso and milk integrate, finishing with a thin, even layer on top. Aim for a smooth surface with little to no dome.

homeMethods.note: Brew a moka pot and froth a small amount of warm milk gently. It's a bold and creamy approximation, though the texture is less silky than steam-wand microfoam.
Press a concentrated shot and whisk or froth warm milk lightly. Pour while swirling. The result is creamy but less glossy than a café version.
Strong coffee and gently frothed milk makes a mellow drink in the right spirit, but it will be milder and not the same as a true flat white.

tips: Smaller amounts of milk heat very fast, so watch temperature closely.
Whole milk gives the silkiest texture.
Flat white size and espresso amount vary by café and country.
commonMistakes: Adding too much air, which makes it a latte or cappuccino.
Using a large cup that waters down the ratio.
Skipping the swirl and tap, leaving bubbles in the milk.

variations.name: Ristretto flat white
variations.description: Uses ristretto shots for a sweeter, more intense taste. Common in some cafés.

variations.name: Oat milk flat white
variations.description: Barista oat milk can create a good microfoam, though results vary by brand.

variations.name: Iced flat white
variations.description: Pour a double shot over ice and top with cold milk for a stronger iced option.

history: The flat white is generally credited to Australia or New Zealand in the 1980s. Which came first is disputed, and both countries claim it.

seo.title: How to Make a Flat White: Silky Microfoam and Double Espresso
seo.description: Learn to make a flat white with 2 oz double espresso and 4 oz steamed milk, plus microfoam tips and no-machine alternatives.
